title: Patch: the changed-cards fuzz rotation plays the Duos wave too

**Issue #4369 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4369: Patch: the changed-cards fuzz rotation plays the Duos wave too
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a pull request changes a card, the fuzz gate already replays that card in extra forced one-on-one games before merge, so a regression in the card is caught the same day. It never does the same for team games: a card that only breaks through a four-seat game (the shared team pool, passes between teammates, concede offers, four mulligans) is dealt only by chance, and a miss waits for the next daily run. After this change, a card change also gets a small bounded set of forced team games on the same pull request.

## Why

- `run()` in the fuzz CLI returns early for `--duos`, before the changed-cards wave; the manual flags refuse the combination too (`--cards` lists `duos` in its conflicts), so even by hand nobody can force cards into Duos games today.
- `play_changed_cards` plays a 1v1 forced wave, a Radiant rotation and changed fused pairs, all one-on-one; the Duos wave has its own endings channel, probes and growth bounds, i.e. the repository already treats team games as a distinct failure domain, but changed cards never enter it per pull request.
- No card script reads team state today, so the risk is not card text branching on teams: it is card hooks meeting engine paths that only exist with four seats (damage routed through the team pool, extra seats owing prompts, concede offers mid-game). Those paths are exactly what random daily deals may never hit for a given card before it merges.
- This does not repeat #1363 (a pinned Duos failure corpus, closed unbuilt): it adds no corpus files and pins no past failure; and it does not repeat #4146 (rejected): no browser is involved.

## Proposal

- Lift the `--cards`/`--duos` conflict so `fuzz --duos --cards <ids>` forces cards into Duos decks, the same way it does for one-on-one decks; keep `--radiant` conflicting with `--duos`, since the Radiant rotation plays run-start games with deck marks and team games have no such path.
- Apply the existing forcing (each token resolved to its carrier, sets dealt several cards a seed) to the four Duos seats' decks, and play a bounded changed-Duos rotation inside `play_changed_cards` with its own summary and coverage lines, capped by new named constants sized for the heavier four-seat games.
- Update the `jackioh-tools` README command table in the same pull request (the acceptance test holds the table to the CLI, so it fails otherwise).

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` (wave orchestration, forcing, new bounds), `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs` (forced Duos decks), `crates/tools/README.md` (command table) and its holding test `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`.
- SPEC §10.7 (the fuzz gate) and SPEC §13 (team games).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --cards <a changed card>` plays Duos games with that card forced into the seats' decks and reports a `changed cards` line; without `--cards` the wave is unchanged.
- [ ] A pull request that changes a card plays the bounded Duos rotation after the 1v1 one, and a seed it fails names the seed, the teams and a `reproduce:` line that replays it.
- [ ] A change with no deckable card still plays nothing extra, and `--radiant --duos` is still refused with the usage error.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` passes, including the acceptance test over the README table.

## Size and risks

Medium: a few hundred lines, mostly the Duos forcing path and its tests. The risk is per-pull-request time (team games cost more than one-on-one ones, and the CI job has an eight-minute budget): keep the new seed cap small and count the rotation's seconds in the pull request. No workflow changes are needed.
```
